From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T11:02:00Z
Subject: RE: Renewal window — prep notes + quick econ calculations

Rachel / Monica —

I pulled a concise set of numbers from the usage dump — short list here so we have talking points for Tue:

Key consumption (2028 Q1–Q2):
- Total tokens: 1.9B tokens (Q2 was 1.1B; Q1 0.8B)
- Chat generation: 48% of tokens (0.92B) — mostly support assistant traffic (peak in May due to new workflow)
- Embeddings: 30% (0.57B) — vector indexing + semantic search on product catalog
- Rerank / scoring: 22% (0.41B) — heavy short-sequence workloads, high qps

Performance notes:
- Median gen latency (p50) stayed steady at ~220ms for typical prompts; p95 shifted 120ms → 170ms in May during a rolling model update (we rerouted to a quantized variant to keep availability)
- Error rate spiked to 1.8% for 6 hours on 2028-05-10 — root cause was a transient GPU OOM in a single shard; no customer-facing data loss observed

Economics / ROI (very rough):
- Flowlytics reports that the rerank pipeline reduced manual review volume by ~52 hours/week across the team. Using their internal $85/hr cost, weekly labor savings ≈ $4.4k → annualized ≈ $230k.
- Q2 bill to Flowlytics (hosted): $42,800 (net of discounts); annualized run-rate at current usage ~ $171k/yr (note Q2 spike inflates this).

Initial commercial options to present:
1) Small commit (+25% tokens) — lowers effective per-token price by ~12%; minimal implementation work.
2) Mid commit + burst credits — 2x baseline tokens reserved, with burst credits for spikes; saves ~18% on unit cost; includes priority routing.
3) Dedicated pool pilot (90-day) — predictable latency improvement (p95 projection down to ~130–140ms), 28% unit cost improvement for heavy rerank throughput, requires SOW + capacity lead time (~6 weeks).

I'll prepare two slides of the math and a short perf trace sample. Monica — can you confirm operational runbook / SLO notes?

—Ben

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

All —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per action items, summarized for procurement and engineering:

1) Operational observations (from Redwood):
- We recommend a short dedicated-pool pilot for the rerank workloads (high qps, low sequence length). Dedicated pilot will reduce variability in p95 by ~35% in our tests and gives you tenant isolation for cache/kv.
- If a pilot is not possible before renewal, the mid-commit + burst credit approach is lower friction and buys headroom through May–June traffic patterns.

2) Implementation checklist (if you pick dedicated):
- Sign SOW (attached) and select pilot window (we'll need 6 weeks to provision and validate).
- Provide list of IP allowlists for the VPC routing and a primary contact for test traffic.

3) Next steps for procurement (Flowlytics):
- I uploaded a compact pricing spreadsheet and draft SOW to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Flowlytics-Shared
- Ben will send the final unit economics and a sample invoice template for the commit option.
